stem.en: Rohan fills all 12,288 numbers of a 64 by 64 picture at random, 1,000 times. He never gets a picture of a ball. Why not?

text.en: The computer has not been taught what a ball is.
A random number from 0 to 255 cannot make red.
A ball needs thousands of pixels to agree.
He needs only a few thousand more tries.

explanation.en: Each random pixel is chosen without looking at its neighbours, but a ball needs a smooth round patch and a plain background all at once. Red is easy to reach and no teaching is involved: a ball picture is possible, only far too rare. The number of possible pictures has 29,593 digits, so a few thousand more tries changes nothing.

hints.en: Think about what one pixel knows about the pixels next to it.
